Studi ital. etc., IV, p. 60 sqq. — Since it has been demonstrated that from the Angelicanus codex the astrological collection of Palchus preserved in the Laurentianus codex, was incompletely copied (Cumont, L'astrologue Palchos, p. 2), we have decided to edit the excerpts from the book of Palchus rather according to the faith of the archetype than of the copy. 2 Concerning Erasistratus cf. above the excerpt of Masala p. 82, l. 23.

summary.headline: Palchus on Lost Objects
summary.text: Introduction to Palchus, a fifth-century Egyptian astrologer, followed by his method for locating a stolen or lost object: the horoskopos, midheaven, setting, and subterranean angles signify the object, owner, thief, and hiding place, while the Moon and planets describe its location and nature.
